instructions: Complete the notes below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
stem_block:
Testing four office layouts

Why firms pick the open-plan option
- Costs less to put up, and is simple to (1) ........ once needs change

The four layouts, each tried for a fortnight
- Plain open-plan, used as the point of comparison
- Zoned open-plan: rooms holding at most 40 staff, shut off by (2) ........ doors
- Activity-based: desks belonging to nobody, plus quiet rooms and shared areas
- Team office: semi-enclosed cubicles for four to six people, screened by (3) ........ panels

How the layouts were judged
- Repeated staff surveys, sensors reading the air and the room, a count of technical output
- Watchers logged everyday habits, for example how often people put on (4) ........

What people did rather than said
- After a spell in the plain open-plan room, desk use in the next layout climbed by roughly 4 per cent
- Read as a genuine preference, not merely a (5) ........ effect

The authors' warning
- Results come from just one company, with a culture and (6) ........ of its own
- Other organisations should try the alternatives on their own staff

items.prompt: Why firms pick the open-plan option: Costs less to put up, and is simple to (1) ........ once needs change
items.evidence: Open-plan arrangements have nonetheless become the default choice for many growing companies, partly because they are cheaper to build and easier to reconfigure than offices divided into permanent rooms.
items.explanation: Paragraf A, açık ofislerin yaygınlaşmasını hem ucuz olmalarına hem de kalıcı duvarlarla bölünmüş ofislere göre daha kolay yeniden düzenlenebilmelerine bağlıyor; bu yüzden cevap 'reconfigure'.

items.prompt: The four layouts: Zoned open-plan: rooms holding at most 40 staff, shut off by (2) ........ doors
items.evidence: Using a Latin square design, in which every team eventually experienced every condition but in a different order, the teams rotated through four distinct office layouts, each for a two-week period: a conventional open-plan office with minimal separation between desks, acting as the baseline; a zoned open-plan design with soundproof doors dividing spaces into rooms holding no more than 40 people; an activity-based design offering unassigned desks alongside dedicated focus rooms and collaboration areas; and a team-office design with large, partly enclosed cubicles seating four to six people behind sound-absorbing panels.
items.explanation: Paragraf B, bölgelendirilmiş açık ofisin ses geçirmez kapılarla en fazla 40 kişilik odalara ayrıldığını söylüyor; kapının niteliği sorulduğu için cevap 'soundproof'.

items.prompt: The four layouts: Team office: semi-enclosed cubicles for four to six people, screened by (3) ........ panels
items.evidence: Using a Latin square design, in which every team eventually experienced every condition but in a different order, the teams rotated through four distinct office layouts, each for a two-week period: a conventional open-plan office with minimal separation between desks, acting as the baseline; a zoned open-plan design with soundproof doors dividing spaces into rooms holding no more than 40 people; an activity-based design offering unassigned desks alongside dedicated focus rooms and collaboration areas; and a team-office design with large, partly enclosed cubicles seating four to six people behind sound-absorbing panels.
items.explanation: Paragraf B, takım ofisinde dört ile altı kişilik yarı kapalı bölmelerin ses emici panellerle çevrildiğini söylüyor; 2. sorudaki 'soundproof' kapılardan farklı olarak burada istenen panel niteliği 'sound-absorbing'.

items.prompt: How the layouts were judged: Watchers logged everyday habits, for example how often people put on (4) ........
items.evidence: As an independent, behavioural proxy for technical output, the researchers also tracked the number of software code commits each team produced, and observers recorded how people actually used the different spaces, noting details such as how often employees wore headphones, retreated to quiet corners, or held impromptu conversations at their desks.
items.explanation: Paragraf C, gözlemcilerin çalışanların ne sıklıkla kulaklık taktığını not ettiğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'headphones'.

items.prompt: What people did rather than said: Read as a genuine preference, not merely a (5) ........ effect
items.evidence: Employees appeared to respond to this with their feet as well as their opinions: once a team's exposure to the open-plan condition ended, desk occupancy in whichever design followed it rose by about 4 per cent, a change the researchers interpreted as a behavioural preference for the newer arrangement rather than simply a novelty effect.
items.explanation: Paragraf F, açık ofisten çıkıldıktan sonra masa doluluğundaki yaklaşık yüzde 4'lük artışın sırf 'yenilik etkisi' değil gerçek bir tercih olarak yorumlandığını söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'novelty'.

items.prompt: The authors' warning: Results come from just one company, with a culture and (6) ........ of its own
items.evidence: They caution, though, that the findings come from a single technology company with its own particular culture and workflows, and that organisations considering a similar redesign would do well to test alternatives with their own staff rather than assume the same ranking will hold everywhere.
items.explanation: Paragraf H, bulguların kendine özgü bir kültürü ve iş akışları olan tek bir teknoloji şirketinden geldiği uyarısını yapıyor; 'culture' zaten verildiği için boşluğa gelen 'workflows'.
